Subject: HIPAA/BAA eligibility + next steps (post-call recap)

Hi Alan / MedCare security team,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear path for HIPAA evaluation and any BAA request.

Recap of what we discussed:
- POI: MedCare will be processing PHI for document ingestion and EHR integration flows.
- Deployment preference: MedCare indicated a preference for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) but wants details on Private (VPC/on-prem) as a potential option.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 report, BAA availability, vendor security questionnaire.

Quick answers / constraints from Redwood:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report available (see attached).
- BAA: We offer a Business Associate Agreement for HIPAA customers, but it is only supported for Dedicated and Private deployment modes. Hosted (public shared) API is not eligible for PHI under our current policy.
- PHI handling boundaries: For HIPAA customers we require one of the eligible deployments above. Typical controls we apply for those deployments include:
  - Dedicated: isolated GPU pools, option to forward audit logs to your SIEM, dedicated tenancy for data at rest separation.
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network, support for KMS/HSM customer keys, full audit log retention controls, and the option to disable telemetry.
  - Encryption: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; customer-managed keys available for Private deployments.

Attachments I'm including: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf (short overview), Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2028.pdf, and a sample Redwood_BAA_Sample.pdf for legal review.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Please send back your completed vendor security questionnaire (or we can take the attached and fill parts).
2) Confirm the scope of PHI you expect to send (endpoints/features: ingestion, EHR sync, webhook responses).
3) Confirm preferred deployment (Dedicated vs Private). If Dedicated, we'll include a short infra appendix; if Private, we'll loop Legal + Eng for onboarding timelines.
4) Once scope and deployment are confirmed, legal teams can start a standard BAA review (typically 2-3 weeks for initial review).

Would you like to schedule a 30-minute follow-up with me and Neha (security) tomorrow or Thursday to go over the questionnaire?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alan — thanks, and appreciate the questionnaire. Quick answers inline and attached items: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2028.pdf and Redwood_BAA_Sample.pdf.

- SOC 2 Type II: Most recent report cover period ended 2028-12-31 (report delivered Q1 2029). That should meet the 'within 12 months' requirement; if you need a signed bridge letter or additional attestations, Neha can coordinate.
- BAA eligibility: Confirmed — BAA is available for Dedicated and Private deployment modes only. Hosted (shared) endpoints are not eligible for processing PHI.
- Dedicated specifics: can provide isolated GPU pools, per-tenant logging that can be forwarded to your SIEM (we commonly support syslog/CloudWatch/EventHub forwarding depending on cloud). There is a capacity provisioning lead time (usually 2-4 weeks from contract + payment to reserved capacity on our standard cadence).
- Private specifics: supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), VPC peering, and optional on-prem package. Onboarding timeline depends on customer infra and legal; typically 4-8 weeks for Private.

Action items from Redwood:
- I attached Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2028.pdf and Redwood_BAA_Sample.pdf for your review.
- Neha (cc'd) will fill any technical addendum fields in the questionnaire and can set up the security deep-dive if you want to go beyond the questionnaire.

Proposed next steps:
1) MedCare returns the questionnaire sections you complete.
2) Confirm chosen deployment (Dedicated vs Private).
3) Legal teams start BAA review after questionnaire and deployment confirmation.

Neha — can you please review the attached questionnaire (Alan) and confirm if we need any additional infra diagrams or logs examples?

Thanks,
Marissa
